title: On Structural Expressive Power of Graph Transformers

problem.claim: The structural expressive power of Graph Transformers needs to be analyzed.

gap.claim: The structural expressive power of Graph Transformers has not been well analyzed.

contributions.claim: Introduces the SEG-WL test, a generalized graph isomorphism test for exploring the structural discriminative power of graph Transformers.

Proves that SEG-WL is an expressivity upper bound for a wide range of graph Transformers and that a simple Transformer network can approximate its representational power arbitrarily under certain conditions.
Develops the Shortest Path Induced Subgraph (SPIS) structural encoding method.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their theoretical findings as providing a novel and practical paradigm for investigating the expressive power of graph Transformers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive synthetic and real-world experiments empirically verify the strengths of the proposed methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Transformers have received wide attention for their performance, but their structural expressive power remains insufficiently analyzed.
The SEG-WL test is introduced as a generalized graph isomorphism test for studying graph Transformer structural discrimination.
SEG-WL is established as an expressivity upper bound for a wide range of graph Transformers, with approximation by a simple Transformer under certain conditions.
The framework connects expressive power to structural encoding design and identifies conditions for exceeding the expressivity of WL tests and GNNs.
A stronger SPIS encoding is developed, and synthetic and real-world experiments are reported to verify the strengths of the proposed methods.

source_observation.claim: The expressive power of graph Transformers is determined by the design of structural encodings.

interpretation.claim: Structural encodings are a central design variable for controlling graph Transformer expressivity.

application.claim: When designing graph Transformers, analyze and compare structural encodings as part of the model's expressivity characterization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which architectural settings or encoding conditions support this application.

source_observation.claim: The authors develop a provably stronger structural encoding method motivated by shortest path distance encoding.

interpretation.claim: Theory-oriented analysis can motivate structural encoding designs intended to improve graph discrimination.

application.claim: Use theoretical expressivity analysis to guide the construction of stronger structural encodings.

exception.claim: The abstract does not define the comparison basis or scope of the claimed stronger expressivity.

unknowns: The specific graph Transformer architectures covered by the upper-bound result are unspecified.
The conditions for arbitrary approximation and for exceeding WL and GNN expressivity are unspecified.
The synthetic and real-world datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The construction and exact theoretical guarantees of SPIS encoding are unspecified.
